title: Refugee or migrant: what is the difference?
examples: What is the difference between a refugee and a migrant?

explain.say: You hear the words migrant and refugee on the news all the time, often mixed up. Are they the same? Look at the board. Two people, side by side. Let us find out what really makes them different.

draw.text: Refugee or migrant: what is the difference?

explain.say: See the left side, migrant? A migrant is anyone who moves to live somewhere else. Usually it is a choice: for a job, to study, or to join family. A migrant can usually go home if they wish. Do you know anyone who moved for work or study?

Now look at the right side, refugee. A refugee is forced to flee war, violence or persecution, and cannot safely go back. That is why a special international law, the 1951 Refugee Convention, protects them. What is the big difference you can spot?

There is one more word: asylum seeker. Asylum means protection. An asylum seeker has asked another country for protection as a refugee and is waiting for a decision. Look at both sides again: which side does an asylum seeker hope to join?

Real life can be messy: some people leave for many reasons at once, and countries argue about how many people to welcome and how. That debate is real and fair to have, but using the right words helps us talk about it clearly. Great work! Challenge: next time you hear these words on the news, check which one fits.

faq.q: What is the difference between a refugee and a migrant?
faq.a: A migrant usually chooses to move, for work, study or family, and can go back. A refugee is forced to flee war or persecution and cannot safely return, so they have special protection in international law.
A migrant is a person who moves from one place to live in another, inside their country or across a border, often for work, study or to be with family.
A refugee is someone who has fled their country because of war, violence or persecution, and who cannot safely go home. The 1951 Refugee Convention protects them.
An asylum seeker is a person who has asked another country for protection as a refugee and is waiting for a decision. If the claim is accepted, they are recognised as a refugee.

faq.q: Why do countries disagree about migration?
faq.a: People weigh different things: some stress the benefits of workers and new ideas or the duty to protect people in danger; others worry about jobs, housing, public services or border control. Each country decides its own migration rules, within international law on refugees.

facts: The 1951 Refugee Convention and its 1967 Protocol have been signed by about 149 countries.
Under the principle of non-refoulement, refugees must not be returned to a country where they face serious threats to their life or freedom.

quiz.say: Amir moves from Egypt to Germany to study engineering. Is he a refugee or a migrant?
quiz.show: Moving abroad to study makes Amir a…
quiz.why: He chose to move for study and can go home, so he is a migrant.

wrong.0: He is not fleeing war or persecution.
wrong.1: He has not asked for protection, he came to study.

quiz.say: What is an asylum seeker waiting for?
quiz.show: An asylum seeker is waiting for…

options.show: A decision on their claim for protection
options.say: A decision on their claim for protection

quiz.why: They have asked for protection as a refugee and wait to hear if it is granted.

wrong.1: Asylum is about protection from danger, not holidays.
wrong.2: Asylum is a claim for safety, not a job application.
